channel.title: Extensible on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Extensible on Best of AI

item.title: Brisk Teaching
item.description:
Teachers can generate lesson materials, adjust reading levels, and draft feedback on student writing. A student-facing feature lets pupils chat with an AI tutor under teacher guidance. It also supports quizzes.

A free plan covers basic features, and paid plans add more. Teachers should check output before using it with students.

MagicSchool and Diffit are alternatives. Brisk Teaching suits educators who work in Google Workspace.

item.title: Deque axe
item.description:
The free axe DevTools browser extension runs on a page and lists issues with the offending element and a suggested fix. The same engine, axe-core, plugs into test frameworks like Cypress, Playwright, and Jest, so teams can catch regressions in continuous integration. Deque’s paid products add guided manual testing and reporting.

Automated checks find only part of all accessibility problems, since things like reading order and meaningful link text need a person. Auditors usually run axe first and then test with a screen reader and keyboard.

item.title: WP Recipe Maker
item.description:
Bloggers enter ingredients and steps, and the plugin outputs schema markup that search engines can read for rich results. It includes nutrition calculation, unit conversion, and ratings. Premium versions add more features.

It requires a WordPress site.

Tasty Recipes and Create by Mediavine are alternatives. WP Recipe Maker suits food bloggers.

item.title: Bardeen
item.description:
Bardeen automates repetitive work that happens on web pages. A user installs the extension, then runs playbooks that click through sites, extract data, and send it elsewhere. Typical uses include scraping lists of people from LinkedIn into Google Sheets, saving a company’s details to a CRM, or sending a meeting summary to Slack.

A natural language builder lets users describe what they want, and the AI assembles the steps, which can be edited. Triggers run automations on a schedule or when something happens, and integrations cover hundreds of apps. Sales and recruiting teams, who spend time moving data between tabs, are heavy users.

item.title: QGIS
item.description:
QGIS gives anyone access to professional-level mapping and spatial analysis at no cost. Users load vector and raster data from files, databases, and web services, style maps, edit geometries, and run analyses such as buffers, overlays, terrain analysis, and routing. A processing toolbox bundles hundreds of algorithms, and it integrates with GRASS and SAGA for specialized tasks. It handles many formats and projections, and print layouts produce publication-quality maps.

The plugin ecosystem is a major strength. Community-developed plugins add functions for data download, cartography, hydrology, field data collection, and more, and Python scripting supports automation. In AI-related work, plugins bring in machine learning for tasks like classifying land cover, detecting objects in imagery, and using models such as Segment Anything for segmentation. Users run QGIS Server to publish maps and QField to collect data on mobile devices.

item.title: Cuey
item.description:
Cuey is a tool for comparing chatbots. From a sidebar in Chrome, you type a prompt once and it goes to services such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini that you are logged into, with the responses displayed together. A view highlights where the answers agree and differ, which is useful for fact-checking and choosing the best phrasing.

It includes a library of saved prompts and a memory feature so context can follow you from one model to another. Because it works with the chat interfaces you already use, it does not need separate API keys. The developer, Llama Valley Inc, states that prompts and responses are not stored on its servers.

item.title: Sider Omni Sidebar
item.description:
Sider began as a browser sidebar for chatting with AI about web pages. Omni Sidebar extends the idea to the whole Mac: a panel that sees the content in the active app and lets users ask questions, summarize, draft replies, or take actions without copying and pasting.

The assistant supports several underlying models and can work with files and screenshots. For people who live in email, documents, and spreadsheets, an assistant that sees the same screen saves steps.

item.title: Codex
item.description:
Codex works as a software engineering agent. A developer describes a task, such as fixing a bug or adding a feature, and Codex explores the code, makes a plan, edits files, and runs tests or linters to verify the result. It reports back with a summary of what it changed and why.

It comes in several forms. A command line tool runs on the developer’s machine, a desktop app manages multiple tasks, extensions integrate with editors like VS Code, and a cloud version in ChatGPT runs tasks in isolated sandboxes, often in parallel, and can propose pull requests on GitHub. Configuration files let teams give the agent project instructions.

item.title: Kiro
item.description:
Kiro is built around spec-driven development. A developer describes a feature, and Kiro produces a requirements document, a technical design, and a task list. The developer reviews and edits these, and the agent then works through the tasks, writing code and tests. The idea is to keep an agent aligned with intent on larger work instead of improvising from chat.

The editor is based on Code OSS, so VS Code extensions and settings carry over. Hooks trigger agent actions on events such as saving a file, steering files give persistent guidance about a project, and support for the Model Context Protocol connects external tools. It uses Claude models through AWS.

item.title: There's An AI For That
item.description:
There’s An AI For That, often shortened to TAAFT, started as a simple search for AI tools by task. A user types what they want to do, such as write a cover letter or remove a background, and gets a list of tools for that job, with ratings and descriptions.

Its size is the draw. It adds new tools constantly, offers an alert for launches, and includes pricing and user reviews. Some listings are promoted by makers.

item.title: AIPRM
item.description:
AIPRM saves people from writing prompts from scratch. Its browser extension adds a prompt library to the ChatGPT interface, organized by topic such as SEO, sales, customer support, productivity, and writing. You pick a prompt template, fill in details like your topic or audience, and it sends a detailed, well-structured instruction to the AI. Users can also create, save, and share their own prompts.

The library grew from community contributions, which means quality varies, though ratings and usage counts help identify useful ones. Paid plans add private prompts, team sharing, and prompt management for organizations, plus integrations with other AI tools. It is popular with marketers and SEO professionals who run the same kinds of tasks repeatedly, such as keyword clustering or content briefs.

item.title: Huntr
item.description:
Huntr helps people stay organized during a job hunt. Users save job postings with a browser extension, move them across stages as they apply and interview, and attach notes, contacts, and documents to each one. Reminders prompt follow-ups so opportunities do not slip.

AI features assist with the writing. They can tailor a resume and cover letter to a posting, suggest keywords, and help prepare for interviews. A resume builder and job board aggregator add to the toolset, and career coaches use Huntr to track clients.

item.title: Lusha
item.description:
Lusha helps sales and recruiting teams get in touch with prospects. While viewing a profile on LinkedIn or a company website, a user clicks the Lusha extension to reveal contact information, then saves it to a CRM. A database search finds contacts by role, company size, and industry.

Additional features include intent signals, technology data, and enrichment of existing lists, as well as integrations with Salesforce, HubSpot, and sales engagement tools. The company emphasizes compliance with privacy laws and offers ways for people to opt out.

item.title: Finch3D
item.description:
Finch3D addresses the early design stage, when architects test many layout ideas against requirements. You define a building footprint or site, along with rules such as unit mix, room sizes, and circulation, and Finch generates floor plan options that satisfy the constraints and optimizes them for factors like area efficiency. Architects can compare alternatives quickly instead of sketching each by hand.

The tool is built to fit architects’ workflows. It integrates with the design software they already use, including Revit, Rhino, and Grasshopper, so generated layouts can be refined and documented in familiar environments. It supports quick iterations when the brief changes, and provides metrics that help justify choices to clients, such as the number of units or usable area.

item.title: NaturalReader
item.description:
NaturalReader turns reading into listening. You paste text, upload a document or PDF, or use the Chrome extension to read a web page, and it reads aloud in a voice you choose, with adjustable speed. Highlighting of each word as it is spoken helps learners follow along, and the tool supports many languages and accents. OCR features can read text from images and scanned pages.

It serves education and accessibility needs. Students with dyslexia, ADHD, or visual impairments use it to access materials, professionals use it to review documents on the go, and teachers use it with classroom content. Premium plans offer higher-quality AI voices, more file formats, and commercial use for creating audio, while a free version covers personal use with basic voices.

item.title: Ultimaker Cura
item.description:
Cura converts 3D models into printer instructions. Users load a model, position it, choose a material and quality profile, and the software slices it into layers, with a preview that shows how the print will be built. Settings control supports, infill, speed, temperature, and more, and a simple mode hides complexity for beginners while a custom mode exposes hundreds of options.

It has a very large user base because it works with many printers, not only those made by UltiMaker. Community-maintained profiles cover popular brands, and a plugin marketplace adds features such as post-processing scripts and cloud integrations. Cura is developed in the open and has had long-running support from the maker community.

item.title: Boomerang
item.description: Boomerang adds time management to Gmail and Outlook. You can write an email and schedule it to send later, set a message to return to your inbox if nobody replies by a certain date, or hide an email until the moment you want to deal with it. Recurring messages, read receipts, and a pause feature that holds incoming mail until you choose to see it help people manage busy inboxes.

item.title: Claude Code
item.description: Claude Code works as an agent on your actual project instead of a suggestion engine in an editor. You start it in a repository from the terminal and describe the task, such as fixing a failing test, adding an endpoint, or upgrading a dependency. It reads the relevant files, makes a plan, edits code across the project, runs tests and other commands, and iterates on the errors. It asks permission for actions that could be risky, and you can review changes as diffs or through git before committing.

item.title: Compose AI
item.description:
Compose AI works wherever you type in Chrome. As you write an email or a message, it suggests the next words or sentence, which you accept with a keystroke, similar to code completion in a programming editor. It can also draft whole replies, rewrite text in a different tone, and fix grammar, with a menu of shortcuts for common tasks.

The product came from a startup that focused on autocomplete for writing, and later added generative features that call large language models for longer tasks. It is intended to save keystrokes on repetitive writing such as emails, support replies, and social posts, and to reduce the effort of starting a draft. A free tier covers basic use, with paid plans for more generations and features.

item.title: Figma
item.description: Figma is where a lot of software gets designed before anyone writes code. It runs in the browser, so designers, product managers, engineers, and writers can open the same file at once, leave comments, and watch changes appear live. That ended the old habit of emailing design files back and forth. Its core strengths are vector editing, Auto Layout for components that resize correctly, and shared libraries that keep colors, type, and buttons consistent across a whole product.

item.title: GitLens AI
item.description:
GitLens enriches VS Code with Git history. It shows inline blame annotations that say who last changed a line, when, and in which commit, and lets you browse the history of a file, line, or branch without leaving the editor. Features include a commit graph, comparisons across branches, and a Launchpad that gathers pull requests and issues. It’s one of the most downloaded extensions for VS Code.

AI features help with common Git chores. GitLens can write commit messages from staged changes, summarize what a commit or branch changed in plain language, and help draft pull request descriptions, saving time on documentation. It supports several AI providers and models, with options for how data is sent.

item.title: GrowthBar
item.description:
GrowthBar tries to simplify SEO for people who are not specialists. You enter a keyword, and the tool shows search volume and difficulty, related keywords, and what the top-ranking pages cover, including their headings and word counts. A Chrome extension displays similar data directly in search results, which helps when researching competitors.

The AI content features turn that research into drafts. GrowthBar can generate outlines, blog posts, and meta descriptions, and tools for rewriting and expanding text help refine them. It also includes rank tracking and backlink data, and an AI assistant to help brainstorm topics. The target users are small business owners, freelancers, and agencies that publish content regularly.

item.title: LANDR
item.description:
LANDR started with automated mastering. An artist uploads a mixed song, the system analyzes it, and an algorithm applies equalization, compression, and loudness adjustments, producing a master in minutes at a price below hiring an engineer. Style and loudness options guide the result.

The company now offers a wider set of services for independent musicians: distribution to streaming platforms, a marketplace of samples, plugins, a collaboration network, and tools for mixing and creating. A subscription bundles many of these.

item.title: Lottie
item.description: Lottie is an animation format created at Airbnb that exports motion from After Effects as small JSON files. The files are vector-based, so they scale to any size without blur, and they are far lighter than GIFs or videos. App and web developers use them for loading spinners, onboarding screens, icons, and illustrations. A Lottie animation can be changed in code, colors can be swapped, and playback controlled, which makes it interactive.

item.title: Mintlify
item.description:
Mintlify helps developer companies publish documentation that looks and works well. Teams write pages in MDX or Markdown, keep them in a Git repository, and Mintlify builds a fast, branded site with navigation, search, code samples, and API playgrounds generated from OpenAPI specs. Many well-known developer tools use it.

AI is part of both the reader and writer experience. An assistant on the docs site answers questions from the documentation, helping users find what they need, and docs are published in forms that AI coding tools can read, such as llms.txt and MCP servers. For writers, AI agents can draft pages, update docs when code changes, and flag outdated content. Analytics show what readers search for and where they get stuck.

item.title: Moz Pro
item.description:
Moz was one of the earliest SEO software companies, and Moz Pro remains a staple for agencies and in-house marketers. Users research keywords, audit sites for technical problems, track rankings over time, and analyze links, with Domain Authority, Moz’s well-known score, used as a quick measure of a site’s strength.

The MozBar browser extension overlays metrics on search results and web pages, making competitor checks quick. Reporting tools produce client-ready summaries, and newer AI features suggest priorities and help with content. A separate local product manages business listings.

item.title: Obsidian
item.description: Obsidian treats notes as local files. Everything you write is a Markdown document in a folder on your computer, so you own the data and can open it with any other editor. You connect notes with links, and the app shows backlinks and a graph view of how ideas relate. People use it for personal knowledge management, research, writing, journaling, and project notes, and many build large networks of thousands of linked notes over years.

item.title: Raycast AI
item.description:
Raycast puts a command bar on your keyboard. Press a hotkey, type a few letters, and you can launch apps, search files, run calculations, manage windows, paste snippets, control music, and use hundreds of extensions that connect to tools such as GitHub, Linear, Notion, and Slack. Power users value how much it can cut mouse use and context switching.

Raycast AI adds chat and commands powered by leading language models. You can ask a question, rewrite selected text, summarize a page, translate, or run custom AI commands from any app, and switch among models from different providers. AI Extensions let the assistant act through extensions, such as creating an issue or checking a calendar, and Model Context Protocol support connects it to more tools. Chats and presets are synced across devices.

item.title: Sheet+
item.description:
Sheet+ is for spreadsheet users who know what they want but not the syntax. You describe the calculation, such as the total of sales for a region in a given month, and Sheet+ produces the formula with an explanation. You can paste a formula you don’t understand and get a plain-language breakdown, or paste an error and receive suggestions for fixing it.

It extends to related tasks. It can write Google Apps Script automation from a description, generate regular expressions, and create SQL queries, and integrates with Sheets through an add-on so you can work without leaving the spreadsheet. It’s popular with small business owners, analysts, and anyone who finds formulas intimidating.

item.title: Tactiq
item.description:
Tactiq takes a lightweight approach to meeting notes. Instead of sending a recording bot into the call, it runs as a browser extension that captures the meeting’s captions and audio on your device. A live transcript appears in a sidebar as people speak, and you can highlight key moments as the meeting happens. That makes it less intrusive in calls where an unfamiliar bot would raise eyebrows.

After the meeting, AI features produce summaries, action items, and custom outputs from prompts, such as a follow-up email or a status update. The transcript is saved in your account and can be exported to tools like Notion, Google Docs, Slack, and HubSpot. Templates adapt the output for different meeting types, and a search function finds past conversations.

item.title: WooCommerce
item.description:
WooCommerce is the most widely used way to run a store on WordPress. You install the plugin, add products, set up payments, shipping, and taxes, and manage orders from the WordPress dashboard. Because it is open source, you own the store and the data, host it where you want, and can modify anything with code or extensions.

The ecosystem is its strength. Thousands of themes and extensions add subscriptions, bookings, memberships, marketplaces, and connections to accounting and marketing tools. AI extensions can write product descriptions, suggest recommendations, and help with support, and Automattic’s own tools plus third-party plugins fill the gaps. Many agencies build custom stores on top of it.

item.title: Guru
item.description:
Guru stores verified knowledge in cards that teams can find where they work. A browser extension and Slack integration surface relevant answers without leaving the page, and experts verify cards on a schedule so that the information stays trustworthy. The idea is a single source of truth for sales, support, and internal teams.

AI search connects to the company’s other sources, such as documents, chat, and ticketing systems, and answers questions in natural language with citations. Analytics show what people search for and which content is stale. Admins control who can see what, and the AI respects those permissions.

item.title: HyperWrite
item.description:
HyperWrite started as a writing tool that predicted and completed text as you typed. It grew into a suite that includes a document editor, a browser extension that works across websites, and tools for rewriting, summarizing, and researching. Users can generate text from prompts and refine it in place.

The company has focused on agents. An assistant can navigate web pages, fill in forms, and complete multi-step tasks in the browser on a user’s behalf, which fits its idea of a personal AI assistant. It supports multiple underlying models.

item.title: MultiOn
item.description:
MultiOn was one of the early companies to build browser-using agents. A user gives an instruction in plain language, and the agent navigates sites, clicks, types, and completes the steps, keeping a session going across pages. Developers could call it through an API to build agents of their own.

The company has talked about moving into a new phase, and directories describe a change of name and focus, though accounts differ. That makes it worth checking the official site to see what is currently available before depending on it.

item.title: Splice
item.description:
Splice supplies the building blocks of modern production. Producers search a huge catalog of samples by genre, key, and tempo, preview them in sync with their project, and download them under a license that allows use in released music. Plugin subscriptions let users rent instruments and effects.

AI features assist with creativity. Tools suggest compatible samples, and apps generate loops and ideas. Cloud project backup and collaboration features help producers work with others.

item.title: Luminar Neo
item.description: Luminar Neo is built for photographers who want strong results without a lot of manual work. Instead of slider-heavy workflows, it offers AI tools that do the hard parts in a click. Sky AI replaces or enhances skies, Relight AI changes the lighting in a scene using depth information, Portrait Bokeh AI creates background blur, and tools for skin, face, and body adjustments handle portraits. Generative tools can erase objects and expand the canvas.
